'''Takabeya Shrine''' (たかべやじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Shimokasuya, {{ill|Isehara, Kanagawa|Q734520|qid=Q734520}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|Q127513|qid=Q127513}}. It is considered one of the 13 Engishiki shrines (minor shrine) in {{ill|Sagami Province|Q1053732|qid=Q1053732}} listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' of Enchō 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}){{sfn|新編相模国風土記稿 下糟屋村 八幡宮}}, though as noted below there are also competing claim shrines ({{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}). Its former shrine rank was Village Shrine.

=== Overview ===
It was formerly the village shrine of {{ill|Takabeya|Q11672972|qid=Q11672972}} in {{ill|Ōsumi district|Q11432367|qid=Q11432367}} with the same shrine name, and was also revered as the general tutelary shrine of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kasuya-shō}}<ref group="注">The place name Kasuya of Kasuya-shō still remains, but note that “Kami'''Kasu'''ya” and “Shimo'''Kasu'''ya” are written with different characters.</ref>, including this district.

Its founding date is unknown. It is listed in the '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}' as one of 13 seats in Sagami Province and was the general tutelary shrine of 127 villages in Ōsumi District. However, {{ill|Takamori Shrine|Q0|qid=Q0|lt=Takamori Shrine}} in Takamori, Isehara, is also considered one of the claim shrines for the Shikinaisha “Takabeya Shrine.” One reason is that this shrine is said to have been called “Takabeya Shrine” before the Meiji-era {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, and inscriptions reading “Takabeya Shrine” remain on timbers and on the back side of the stone monument beside its {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}}<ref>[http://w1.oroti.net/~takamori/htdocs/ Sagami no Kuni Takamori Shrine] (official website), history page.</ref>.

In the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, Kasuya Tōta Saemon no Jō Arisue ({{ill|Kasuya Arisue|Q11604765|qid=Q11604765}}), a retainer of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ar|ميناموتو نو يوريتومو|be|Мінамота-но Ёрытома|bg|Минамото но Йоритомо|br|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ca|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ckb|مینامۆتۆ نۆ یۆریتۆمۆ|cs|Joritomo Minamoto|de|Minamoto no Yoritomo|el|Μιναμότο νο Γιοριτόμο|eo|Minamoto no Yoritomo|es|Minamoto no Yoritomo|eu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fa|میناموتو نو یوریتومو|fi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|hak|Minamoto no Yoritomo|he|מינאמוטו נו יוריטומו|hu|Minamoto no Joritomo|id|Minamoto no Yoritomo|it|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝|ko|미나모토노 요리토모|la|Minamoto no Yoritomo|lt|Minamoto no Joritomo|mr|मिनामोटो नो योरिमोटो|ms|Minamoto no Yoritomo|nl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|pl|Yoritomo Minamoto|pt|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ro|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ru|Минамото-но Ёритомо|sh|Minamoto no Yoritomo|sk|Joritomo Minamoto|sl|Minamoto no Joritomo|sq|Minamoto no Joritomo|sr|Минамото но Јоритомо|sv|Minamoto no Yoritomo|th|มินาโมโตะ โนะ โยริโตโมะ|tl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|tr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|uk|Мінамото-но Йорітомо|vi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|war|Minamoto no Yoritomo|wuu|源赖朝|zh|源赖朝|zh_min_nan|Minamoto no Yoritomo|zh_yue|源賴朝|zu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800}} and local {{ill|Jitō|Q1329805|qid=Q1329805}} of Kasuya-shō, built a new shrine building with Takabeya Shrine as his guardian deity. A bronze bell made in Shitoku 3 ({{ill|1386|Q6355|qid=Q6355}}) December by Munekuni, governor of Kawachi, and donated by Taira Hidenori is designated an Important Cultural Property of Kanagawa Prefecture. In Tenbun 20 ({{ill|1551|Q6560|qid=Q6560}}), local jitō Watanabe Iwami-no-kami restored the shrine buildings{{sfn|新編相模国風土記稿 下糟屋村 八幡宮}}. In Tenshō 19 ({{ill|1591|Q6766|qid=Q6766}}) November, it received a red-seal grant of 10 koku of shrine land from {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}}{{sfn|新編相模国風土記稿 下糟屋村 八幡宮}}. Until around the mid-Edo period, it was also called “Kasuya Hachimangū.”

The main sanctuary was rebuilt in Shōhō 4 ({{ill|1647|Q6935|qid=Q6935}}), but collapsed in the {{ill|aftermath of 1923 Great Kantō earthquake|Q3742341|qid=Q3742341}}; in Shōwa 4 ({{ill|1929|Q18792|qid=Q18792}}) it was rebuilt reusing the columns, carvings, and front doors. The worship hall was rebuilt in Keiō 1 ({{ill|1865|Q7708|qid=Q7708}}).

The shrine preserves three old gagaku masks used in rituals from the Kamakura period onward, and a plaque reading “Hachimangū” written in early Genroku by Etsuzan Dōsō, the 7th abbot of {{ill|Manpuku-ji|Q576318|qid=Q576318}} (Ōbaku-zan, Uji, Kyoto), a monk who came from Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, China. Gyōan and Gyōhaku, who donated the komainu in front of the main sanctuary, were also monks of the {{ill|Ōbaku|Q384728|qid=Q384728}}, suggesting a period of strong ties with Ōbaku along with the former bettō temple Jingū-ji.

At present it is concurrently administered by {{ill|Isehara Daijingu|Q11378955|qid=Q11378955}}, where one may also receive {{ill|Shuin|Q7504772|qid=Q7504772|lt=seal stamps}}.

=== History ===
* {{ill|1551|Q6560|qid=Q6560}} (Tenbun 20) - Shrine buildings rebuilt by local {{ill|Jitō|Q1329805|qid=Q1329805}} Watanabe Iwami-no-kami.
* {{ill|1591|Q6766|qid=Q6766}} (Tenshō 19) - 10-koku red-seal grant donated by Tokugawa Ieyasu.
* {{ill|1865|Q7708|qid=Q7708}} (Keiō 1) - Shrine buildings restored.
* {{ill|1923|Q2169|qid=Q2169}} (Taishō 12) - Main sanctuary collapsed in the {{ill|aftermath of 1923 Great Kantō earthquake|Q3742341|qid=Q3742341}}.
* {{ill|1929|Q18792|qid=Q18792}} (Shōwa 4) - Main sanctuary rebuilt.

=== Rituals ===
[[File:Takabeya-jinja(Isehara) Kaguraden.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Kagura hall]]
A ritual called “Shiokumi no Shinji” has been held in September for over 1,000 years since the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}. The beach sand used in the rite is taken from Terugasaki Coast, where {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|lt=Sumiyoshi Ōkami|qid=Q1114013}} (Ōsumi Daimyōjin) is said to have landed. Until around the early {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} period, the shrine duty group and priest walked the 16 {{ill|Kilometre|Q828224|qid=Q828224|lt=km}} one way to Terugasaki to collect seawater, beach sand, and hondawara seaweed (sargassum). The seawater is used as fire-quelling sacred water; the beach sand is spread on the approach for purification; the hondawara is hung on shimenawa at the worship hall and torii.

=== Precincts ===
Within the precincts are the main sanctuary, worship hall, {{ill|Kagura-den|Q94498|qid=Q94498}}, purification place, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=temizuya}}, {{ill|Bonshō|Q8192099|qid=Q8192099|lt=temple bell}}, playground equipment, and the following precinct shrines.

=== National Registered Tangible Cultural Properties ===
; Main sanctuary
: Collapsed in the Great Kantō Earthquake and rebuilt in Shōwa 4. Most major timbers are reused from the pre-collapse main sanctuary rebuilt in {{ill|Shōhō|Q1146192|qid=Q1146192}} 4 (1647). Registered as a National Registered Tangible Cultural Property on February 25, 2016.
; Worship hall
: Rebuilt in Keiō 1 (1865). Like the main sanctuary, registered as a National Registered Tangible Cultural Property on February 25, 2016.

=== Important Cultural Property of Kanagawa Prefecture ===
; Bell tower
: In {{ill|Shitoku|Q1146202|qid=Q1146202|lt=Shitoku}} 3 (1386) December, Taira Hidenori donated a bronze bell. The bell is designated an Important Cultural Property of Kanagawa Prefecture.

=== Access ===
* About 20 minutes on foot from {{ill|Isehara Station|arz|محطة ايسيهارا|fr|Gare d'Isehara|it|Stazione di Isehara|ja|伊勢原駅|ko|이세하라역|my|အိဆဲဟရဘူတာ|ru|Исэхара (станция)|ur|ایسہارا اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢原站|qid=Q4205219}} on the {{ill|Odakyū Odawara Line|de|Odakyū Odawara-Linie|es|Línea Odakyu Odawara|fa|خط اوداکیو-اوداوارا|fr|Ligne Odakyū Odawara|it|Linea Odakyū Odawara|ja|小田急小田原線|ko|오다큐 오다와라선|nl|Odawara-lijn|ru|Линия Одавара (Одакю)|th|รถไฟฟ้าโอดะกีวสายโอดาวาระ|zh|小田原線|qid=Q135176}}.
* Bus from the station north exit on {{ill|Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|ja|神奈川中央交通|ko|가나가와 중앙 교통|qid=Q10854960}}:
** {{ill|I76 route|ja|神奈川中央交通伊勢原営業所|qid=Q11588882}} bound for {{ill|Aikō-Ishida Station|arz|محطة ايكو ايشيدا|it|Stazione di Aikō-Ishida|ja|愛甲石田駅|ko|아이코이시다역|my|အအိခိုး − အိရှိဒဘူတာ|ru|Аико-Исида|ur|آئی کو-ایشیڈا اسٹیشن|zh|爱甲石田站|qid=Q1107009}}, get off at “Kasuya-Kamijuku,” 3-minute walk.
** {{ill|I74 route|ja|神奈川中央交通伊勢原営業所|qid=Q11588882}} bound for Aiko-Ishida Station, get off at “Awakubo Iriguchi,” 4-minute walk.
